design_goal: extend the local visual system through typography, spacing, component rhythm, and responsive layout
problem_statement: brunoimbrizi/interactive-particles is a runnable three.js (r98) WebGL Codrops demo built with webpack that draws a large interactive particle field on a full-viewport canvas; clicking the canvas cycles through five particle source images and pressing G toggles a ControlKit tuning panel. It is restyled here as the fictional 'Ember Drift' generative-motion studio (artist Sable Verrine), whose five source images become the studio's five signal plates. Over the fixed full-viewport particle canvas floats Ember Drift's own foreground instrument, the 'Signal deck' (a .deck panel): an eyebrow wordmark, a title, a subtitle, two workflow step lines, a plate selector chip row (All plates, Plate 01 through Plate 05), a strip of the five plate thumbnails, and a live readout beneath the chips that reads 'Now drifting: All plates · 5 plates staged'. The signal deck is the only normal-flow foreground chrome — the WebGL canvas itself is a fixed inset:0 layer that never scrolls — so the deck carries all responsive, visual, cross-context and interaction behaviour. The task is to finish the signal deck so it is a single coherent, legible, responsive control instrument: (1) the plate chip row must wrap cleanly and never force horizontal overflow on a 390px phone; (2) the deck must stay legible and well-proportioned over the field rather than overgrowing its chips and thumbnails into oversized dark slabs that cascade, overlap and bury the readout with dark-on-dark text; (3) the signal deck must persist as the same instrument across every context the operator moves into (the stage view, the drift console open, and the field-drifting trail), not vanish once the console is opened or the field starts drifting; and (4) picking a plate in the chip row must update the readout live (e.g. picking Plate 02 must change the readout to 'Now drifting: Plate 02 · 1 plate on view'), not leave a frozen 'All plates' line while the chip merely highlights. The WebGL particle field, its GLSL shaders, the canvas-click sample cycling, the G-key ControlKit toggle, the five source images, the frame masthead and Codrops links must remain fully intact.
required_content: The Ember Drift Signal deck (the .deck panel) renders over the WebGL particle field with its eyebrow wordmark, title, subtitle, workflow step lines, plate selector chip row, thumbnail strip and live readout, and stays legible and well-proportioned rather than overgrowing its chips and thumbnails into oversized slabs that cascade, overlap and bury the readout with illegible dark-on-dark text.
The plate selector chip row wraps cleanly and introduces no horizontal overflow of the foreground chrome on a 390px mobile viewport.

The signal deck persists as one consistent instrument across every context the operator moves into — the stage view, the drift console open, and the field-drifting trail — not appearing only on the initial stage view.

Selecting a plate in the selector updates the readout live to name the chosen plate (for example 'Now drifting: Plate 02 · 1 plate on view'); the active chip highlight and the readout stay in sync rather than the readout freezing on the initial 'All plates' line.
The three.js WebGL particle field, its GLSL shaders, the canvas-click sample cycling, the G-key ControlKit tuning toggle and the five particle source images remain fully intact and reachable.
The restyled Ember Drift persona (masthead wordmark, deck title/subtitle, workflow copy and the five plate thumbnails) is preserved and reads as one coherent generative-motion-studio narrative.
design_constraints: Preserve the demo's immersive full-viewport WebGL identity: the particle canvas fills the screen and the signal deck overlay remains the only foreground chrome, keeping the Ember Drift teal/magenta ember theme, its Futura typography and its translucent card styling over the dark ground.

Do not convert the experience into a marketing landing page, dashboard, blog, or multi-section scrolling site; it must remain a single-route immersive particle canvas with a floating signal deck overlay.

The plate selector chip row must be a responsive, wrapping, self-clamping flex layout (chips flex 1 1 auto, min-width 0) with consistent spacing so it never exceeds the mobile viewport width; do not use a fixed wide no-wrap row.

The deck chips, thumbnails, labels and readout must keep sufficient visual contrast to stay legible over the field; do not set near-black text on near-black chip fills or let the chip cards and thumbnails overlap one another in a colliding pile.
Keep the deck card's density and spacing compact and legible at desktop, tablet and mobile breakpoints, sizing the chip and thumbnail cards so they sit inside the overlay without clipping.
The signal deck must be mounted in every context (stage / tune / trail) so it reads as one persistent instrument, not only on the initial stage view.
The plate selector's readout must be derived live from the selected plate each render, so a click updates both the active chip highlight and the readout text together.
state_constraints: desktop_initial, tablet_initial and mobile_initial capture the particle field with the Signal deck floating over it at 1440px, 834px and 390px; on mobile the plate chip row must wrap and stay free of horizontal overflow.

desktop_second_sample and desktop_third_sample frame the deck after the operator picks Plate 02 / Plate 03 in the selector; the deck must be legible and well-proportioned, not an overgrown cascade of dark slabs, and the readout must update to name the chosen plate rather than stay frozen on 'All plates'.

desktop_panel_expanded and desktop_particle_trail capture the operator opening the drift console and letting the field drift; the signal deck must persist across these contexts, not vanish after the stage view.
mobile_second_sample captures the same plate pick on a 390px phone; the deck must remain overflow-free and its readout must update live.
In the original demo there is no signal deck; the deck is the restyled foreground instrument, and the WebGL particle field, shaders, source images and canvas interactions are polished and preserved.

change_completion: The Ember Drift Signal deck renders with its wordmark, title, subtitle, workflow steps, plate selector chip row, thumbnail strip and live readout over the particle field.
Selecting a plate updates the readout live to name the chosen plate rather than leaving a frozen 'All plates' readout while only the chip highlights.
design_consistency: The signal deck stays legible and well-proportioned over the field, with contrasting chip and thumbnail text and non-overlapping chips, preserving the Ember Drift teal/magenta ember palette.
The signal deck persists as one consistent instrument across the stage, tune and trail contexts rather than only the initial stage view.
regression: The three.js particle field renders full-viewport and the canvas-click sample cycling, G-key ControlKit toggle and five source images remain functional across all legs.
The restyled Ember Drift persona wordmark, deck title and workflow copy are preserved by any acceptable solution.
responsive: The 390px and 834px states show no horizontal overflow of the signal deck chrome.
The plate selector chip row wraps cleanly on mobile so its chips stack instead of forcing a wide no-wrap row.

author_notes: Repo-grounded webpack three.js WebGL particle demo (brunoimbrizi/interactive-particles) restyled as the Ember Drift generative-motion studio. The native lever is the studio's own on-canvas Signal deck (the .deck panel with a plate selector chip row, a thumbnail strip and a live readout). Because the particle canvas is a fixed inset:0 layer with zero scrollWidth, the signal deck is the sole normal-flow foreground chrome and carries all four graded behaviours: responsive no-overflow of the chip row, legible non-overgrown visual design, cross-context persistence of the deck, and a live plate-selector readout. The deck context is switched deterministically in capture via a window.__ember hook exposed identically in all legs (infrastructure, not the restyle). The WebGL field renders under swiftshader; GPU ReadPixels stalls are warnings, not errors. Five plate thumbnail images (sample-01.png through sample-05.png) and their alt text are preserved assets. DESIGN_KEYWORDS: ember, drift, generative, signal, particles, motion.
